newsitem.title: USA: Calif Nov. home sales up 6.4 pct in 1996 - Realtors.
newsitem.headline: Calif Nov. home sales up 6.4 pct in 1996 - Realtors.

text.p: The pace of California home sales increased 6.4 percent in November from a year earlier, but slowed from October's pace, the California Association of Realtors reported on Monday.

On a seasonally-adjusted, annualized basis, 497,270 existing, single-family detached homes closed escrow in California during November, up from the annualized rate in November 1995, the association said in a report.
But the pace of November sales was 1.2 percent slower than the revised annualized rate of 503,110 homes sold in October, the report said.
Statewide home sales for the first 11 months of the year rose 20 percent from January-November, 1995, the association said.

Median home prices rose during November from a year ago in 136 of more than 300 selected California cities, the association said. The statewide median price of an existing, single-family detached home sold during November was $175,500, up 0.8 percent from $174,100 in October.
The November median price edged down 0.4 percent from November 1995, when the median-priced home sold for $176,200, the association said.

Fixed mortgage interest rates averaged 7.58 percent during November, down from an average of 7.89 percent in October. "These favorable mortgage rates will likely spark additional demand for housing throughout California as we move into 1997," association President Bob Kulick said.
